anti_overlap: Does not review token accounting accuracy (fd-compute-metering) or CRDT merge mechanics (fd-crdt-state-merging). Focuses exclusively on permission and governance rule design, not economics or technical state.
decision_lens: Every governance primitive is evaluated against: can this be abused, can it be audited, can it be changed safely, and does it degrade gracefully when participants act in bad faith?
focus: Reviews whether the permission and role model is sound, auditable, and resistant to governance capture or privilege escalation
name: fd-governance-permission-model
persona: Platform governance architect with deep experience designing permission systems for multi-tenant collaborative platforms (GitHub, Notion, Figma enterprise)
review_areas: Role model completeness — does Owner/participant binary cover real-world scenarios like delegated moderators, read-only observers, or temporary elevated access for agents?
Governance capture risk — can an Owner lock out co-owners, transfer ownership unilaterally, or install governance rules that make themselves irremovable?
Policy enforcement boundary — the design says gardens declare rules but the platform enforces them; are there gaps where declared rules can be circumvented at the platform layer?
Transition safety — when a garden switches governance models (Solo → Cooperative), what happens to in-flight directions, existing attributions, and cached permissions?
Agent role ambiguity — agents contribute compute but are they participants, tools of participants, or a third role class? The design is silent on agent identity in the permission model.
Audit trail coverage — are governance rule changes themselves attributed and versioned, or only contributions to content directions?

severity_examples.condition: The design has no succession mechanism. A sole-owner garden where the owner disappears creates an unresolvable governance deadlock — no one can merge directions, modify the constitution, or wind down the garden.

'Bring your own compute' means agents run under a participant's API key. If an agent accrues attribution under a participant's identity, that participant gains voting weight or revenue share they did not personally contribute. The design does not distinguish human-authored vs agent-authored contributions under a shared identity.
No migration path is specified. If a garden mid-direction switches from Solo to Cooperative, the authority to merge or abandon that direction is suddenly ambiguous.
severity_examples.scenario: Governance model migration with active directions

success_hints: A sound permission model names every actor class (human owner, human participant, agent-as-tool, agent-as-participant), defines what each can do and cannot do, specifies who can change the rules and under what conditions, and provides a fallback when governance is contested or the owner is absent.
task_context: Garden Salon governance brainstorm covering roles, directions, attribution primitives, and an evolutionary path from emergent usage to formal constitutions. 'Bring your own compute' model where contributors supply API keys.
